title: Koszul dual of a Koszul-regular immersion
statement: Let Y be a Noetherian scheme [def-pc-scheme], and let i:Z\to Y be a Koszul-regular closed immersion [def-weil-closed-immersion, def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let C_i be its conormal sheaf [def-sbc-closed-immersion-ideal-sheaf, def-pc-module-pullback], let N_i:=\operatorname{SheafHom}_{\mathcal O_Z}(C_i,\mathcal O_Z) be its normal sheaf [def-pur-sheaf-hom], and let r be the locally constant rank of C_i. If a is the right adjoint of Ri_*:D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)\to D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Y) [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-derived-direct-image], then there is a canonical isomorphism \bigwedge^r N_i[-r]\cong a(\mathcal O_Y) in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z).

proof.text: Use the determinant quasi-coherence theorem to regard the explicit rank-stratified normal determinant D as an object of D_QCoh(Z). A closed immersion is finite. Mathlib finite-type and quasi-compact facts make Z Noetherian; OY is bounded below in degree zero. Supply a standard chosen derived category over the direct-image algebra.

Choose the ambient scalar right adjoint H from the affine derived Hom theorem. Apply finite_duality_derived_hom to the given geometric adjunction, its definitional direct-image comparison, and H. Its algebra-valued component identifies Rg_*a(OY) with H(OY). The algebra-linear Koszul theorem identifies Rg_*D with H of the degree-zero structure sheaf. Transport through hOY and compose to obtain Rg_*D≅Rg_*a(OY), before any scalar restriction.

Take the affine derived equivalence E and its natural comparison with Rg_*. Compose its component at D, the previous algebra-derived isomorphism and the inverse component at a(OY). Lift first through the fully faithful full-subcategory inclusion D_QCoh(A)→D(A), then through E.fullyFaithfulFunctor. This gives D≅a(OY), together with its quasi-coherence witness.
